newsitem.title: USA: Maytag sees slow start to '97 performance.
newsitem.headline: Maytag sees slow start to '97 performance.

text.p: Maytag Corp said Thursday it expects its 1997 earnings performance to start slowly, but pick up after mid-year.

"Looking ahead for 1997, we see continued strong performance for the Hoover brand, combined with improved performance in major appliances and at Dixie-Narco," Leonard Hadley, chairman, said in a statement. "We expect to introduce a key new Hoover product line in the second half, and that will add momentum later in the year."
Maytag said it expects to introduce a new refrigerator line in February and a new horizontal axis washing machine in March.

"Overall, we expect our earnings performance to start slowly but to pick up after mid-year, when much of the sales and earnings impact from these product introductions will begin to be realized," Hadley said.
Maytag makes home appliances. Its Dixie-Narco unit is a vending equipment manufacturer.

Earlier, Maytag reported earnings for the fourth quarter of $0.36 a share, compared with $0.29 a year ago before charges. For the year, it earned $1.60 a year before charges compared with 1995 earnings of $1.35 before charges.

"Our operating performance again was led by the Hoover brand, which posted record results for the year," Hadley said. "The joint venture with RSD in China, which we announced in September 1996, also contributed positively to the corporation's results, and we continue to be very enthusiastic about that business opportunity."
In September, Maytag said it would invest about $70 million in a series of joint ventures with the Heifei Rongshida Group, known as RSD, in China.
Maytag said lower raw material costs in 1996 also helped the company's performance.

Sales of major appliances overall increased in the fourth quarter, consistent with industry-wide growth. For the full year, sales of major appliances were flat with 1995 levels. Maytag and Jenn-Air premium brands performed well during the year, but value brands were off, it added.
Maytag said its Hoover floor care posted double-digit gains in sales in the fourth quarter and the year.
In commercial laundry equipment, sales increased during the year as did Maytag's market share.
At Dixie-Narco, fourth quarter sales of $30.4 million were down 24 percent, and sales from ongoing operations dropped 16 percent. Operating income was break-even for the quarter.
For 1996, Dixie-Narco's sales declined 17 percent to $162.3 million and operating income fell 54 percent to $10.7 million. Sales from ongoing operations were down nine percent.
Dixie-Narco expects improved performance in 1997, Maytag said, with strong orders and lower production costs.
